Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.

class GameTimerScheduler
  class << self
    def schedule(game_id:, game_question_id:, closes_at:)
      return unless closes_at

      delay = [ closes_at.to_f - Time.current.to_f, 0.0 ].max + 0.005
      target_mono = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + delay

      mutex.synchronize do
        deadlines[[ game_id.to_i, game_question_id.to_i ]] = target_mono
        ensure_worker_running_locked
        cv.broadcast
      end
    end

    def cancel(game_id:, game_question_id:)
      mutex.synchronize do
        deadlines.delete([ game_id.to_i, game_question_id.to_i ])
      end
    end

    def restore_pending!
      Game.where(status: "question_open").includes(:current_game_question).find_each do |game|
        gq = game.current_game_question
        next unless gq&.closes_at

        if Time.current >= gq.closes_at
          game.expire_open_question_if_due!(expected_game_question_id: gq.id)
        else
          schedule(game_id: game.id, game_question_id: gq.id, closes_at: gq.closes_at)
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.error("GameTimerScheduler.restore_pending! failed: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def cv
      @cv ||= ConditionVariable.new
    end

    def deadlines
      @deadlines ||= {}
    end

    def ensure_worker_running_locked
      return if @worker&.alive?

      @worker = Thread.new { run_loop }
      @worker.name = "quizzy-game-timer"
      @worker.abort_on_exception = false
      @worker.report_on_exception = false
    end

    def run_loop
      loop do
        due_key = nil

        mutex.synchronize do
          while deadlines.empty?
            cv.wait(mutex)
          end

          key, earliest_mono = deadlines.min_by { |_, mono| mono }
          now_mono = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

          if earliest_mono > now_mono
            cv.wait(mutex, earliest_mono - now_mono)
          else
            deadlines.delete(key)
            due_key = key
          end
        end

        process_due(due_key[0], due_key[1]) if due_key
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.error("GameTimerScheduler worker error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      sleep 0.05
      retry
    end

    def process_due(game_id, game_question_id)
      Rails.application.executor.wrap do
        game = Game.find_by(id: game_id)
        next unless game&.question_open? && game.current_game_question_id == game_question_id

        gq = game.current_game_question
        next unless gq&.closes_at

        if Time.current < gq.closes_at
          schedule(game_id: game_id, game_question_id: game_question_id, closes_at: gq.closes_at)
        else
          game.expire_open_question_if_due!(expected_game_question_id: game_question_id)
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.error("GameTimerScheduler.process_due error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    end
  end
end

          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body
          }
        end
      else
        counts = gq.answers.group(:option_id).count
        total_answers = counts.values.sum
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          cnt = counts[opt.id] || 0
          share = total_answers.positive? ? ((cnt.to_f / total_answers) * 100).round(1) : 0
          {

            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?,
            count: cnt,
            share: share
          }

      payload[:number_of_winners] = quiz.number_of_winners
      payload[:leaderboard] = resolved_entries.map do |entry|
        {

          place: entry[:place],
          name: entry[:name],
          points: entry[:points],
          winner: entry[:winner]
        }

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title
    }

    if (question_open? || question_closed?) && (gq = current_game_question)
      question = gq.question
      opts = question.options.to_a
      total = game_questions.count

      payload[:total_questions] = total
      payload[:question_body] = question.body

      if question_open?
        # Strictly exclude correctness while question is open!
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body
          }
        end
      else
        payload[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            letter: option_letter(idx),
            body: opt.body,
            correct: opt.correct?
          }
        end
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_state_payload_for(player, entries: nil)
    payload = public_player_broadcast_payload.dup
    payload[:joined] = player.present?
    payload[:player_name] = player&.name

    if player.present? && (question_open? || question_closed?) && (gq = current_game_question)
      payload[:picked_option_id] = gq.answers.find_by(player_id: player.id)&.option_id
    elsif player.present? && finished?
      resolved_entries = entries || leaderboard_entries
      entry = resolved_entries.find { |e| e[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        payload[:place] = entry[:place]
        payload[:total_players] = resolved_entries.size
        payload[:points] = entry[:points]
        payload[:winner] = entry[:winner]
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def schedule_question_timer(gq_id, closes_at)
    return unless gq_id && closes_at

    game_id = id
    ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do

        game_id: game_id,
        game_question_id: gq_id,
        closes_at: closes_at
      )
    end
  end

  def option_letter(index)
    index < 26 ? ("A".ord + index).chr : (index + 1).to_s
  end

  def assign_code
    return if code.present?

    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
        self.code = candidate
        break
      end
    end
  end

cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application using SQLite (`storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, Turbo, Stimulus, Action Cable, Solid Cache, and Solid Queue (all configured to store data exclusively under `storage/` with zero external service calls).

## Boot & Production Serving (`bin/serve`)

- `bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` and `PORT` (default `3000`), precompiles assets (`bin/rails assets:precompile`), prepares SQLite databases (`bin/rails db:prepare` across `primary`, `cache`, `queue`, and `cable`), and runs a single multi-threaded Puma process in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP is used (`config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`), all hostnames are accepted (`config.hosts.clear`), and Action Cable origin forgery checks are disabled (`config.action_cable.disable_request_forgery_protection = true`) so HTTP and WebSockets accept any `Host` / `Origin`.
- Because Puma runs as a single foreground process (`config/puma.rb`), Action Cable uses the in-memory `async` adapter in `config/cable.yml` with a 16-thread worker pool (`config.action_cable.worker_pool_size = 16`), delivering question and winner broadcasts to big screens and phones in sub-millisecond time without SQLite polling jitter.
- `GET /up` serves the public health check (`200 OK`).
- Every route under `/moderate` inherits from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Authentication against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]`.

## Data Model

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized), `number_of_winners` (integer >= 1, default `3`), `timer_minutes` (integer >= 0, default `0`), `timer_seconds` (integer `0..59`, default `0`), all editable via Quiz Settings. `0` minutes and `0` seconds (`timer_duration_seconds == 0`) means no timer. Has many `games`, `questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, and `active_questions` (`where(active: true)`).
  - `Quiz#as_export_json` / `Quiz#to_export_json` exports strictly `{"title", "questions" => [{"text", "active", "options" => [{"text", "correct"}]}]}` in order, omitting instance settings (`number_of_winners`, `timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`), database IDs, timestamps, and runtime session/game data.
- `QuizImport` (`app/models/quiz_import.rb`): parses and validates quiz JSON (`active` defaults to `true`, `correct` defaults to `false`, enforcing all question form rules) and creates the new `Quiz` (`number_of_winners` defaults to `3`, `timer_minutes` and `timer_seconds` default to `0`), `Question`s, and `Option`s atomically inside a single database transaction.
- `Question` (`questions`): belongs to `quiz`; `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (integer). Has many `options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
- `Option` (`options`): belongs to `question`; `body` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer).
- `Game` (`games`): belongs to `quiz`; `code` (unique 5-char uppercase alphanumeric code), `status` (`"lobby"`, `"question_open"`, `"question_closed"`, `"finished"`), `current_question_index`, `current_game_question_id`, `state_version` (monotonic counter), `started_at`, `finished_at`.
  - `start!` snapshots `quiz.active_questions` in order into `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`: `position` `1..N`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`, `duration_seconds`, `closes_at`), skipping inactive questions.
  - `finish_question!`, `expire_open_question_if_due!`, `next_question!`, `end_quiz!`, `pick_top_winners!`, `draw_winners!`, and `reset_winners!` mutate state under `with_lock` and broadcast synchronously over Action Cable.
- `Player` (`players`): belongs to `game`; `name` (required, whitespace-normalized), `token` (secret token stored in signed HTTP-only cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>` so reopening `/play/<CODE>` in the same browser continues as the same player), `online` (boolean), `last_seen_at`, `winner` (boolean, default `false`).
  - `PlayerConnection` (`player_connections`): tracks active WebSocket `connection_uid`s per player so multi-tab sessions stay online until all tabs disconnect (`unsubscribed` + `pagehide` teardown + `ONLINE_TTL` heartbeat).
- `Answer` (`answers`): unique per `(game_question_id, player_id)`; stores `option_id` and microsecond-precision `answered_at` (captured on request arrival before lock wait, updating in place when a player changes their pick while the question is open so the last pick counts).

## Per-Question Timer

- When a question opens (`start!` or `next_question!`) on a quiz with `timer_duration_seconds > 0`, `GameQuestion` records `opened_at = now`, `duration_seconds`, and `closes_at = now + duration_seconds.seconds`.
- **Big-Screen Display Only**: `Game#moderator_state_payload` includes relative `timer_duration_seconds` and `timer_remaining_ms` (`closes_at - Time.current`) only while `status == "question_open"`, rendered inside `.screen` as `.stage-timer` in `M:SS` format (`"1:30"`, `"0:05"`). Because `closes_at` is persisted in SQLite and relative `timer_remaining_ms` is computed on the server, reloading the page never restarts the countdown and avoids client/server clock skew. Players never see or receive timer fields in HTML, JSON, or WebSocket broadcasts.
- **Auto-Finish at `0:00`**: `GameTimerScheduler` (`app/models/game_timer_scheduler.rb`) maintains an in-process `ConditionVariable` timer thread scheduled via `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` (and restored on Puma boot via `after_booted`) that calls `Game#expire_open_question_if_due!(expected_game_question_id:)` at `closes_at`, closing the question and broadcasting over Action Cable identically to clicking `"Finish"`. `submit_answer!` and HTTP/WebSocket state reads also enforce `expire_open_question_if_due!`, and clicking `"Finish"` early cancels the scheduled timer for that `game_question_id`.

## Scoring, Leaderboard & Prizes

- **Scoring**: Each correct final answer gives `1` point. Equal points are broken by lower total elapsed time (`answered_at.to_r - opened_at.to_r`, exact Rational arithmetic) across correct answers only, with `player.id` as final deterministic tie-breaker. Points and places are hidden from players until `status == "finished"`.
- **Finished Views**:
  - Big screen renders `<ol class="leaderboard">` with one `<li class="leader">` per player in rank order showing place, name (plus `<span class="leader__badge">Winner</span>` when `winner`), and points (`"2 points"`, `"1 point"`, `"0 points"`).
  - Joined player phones render `.result-card` showing `"Place X of Y"`, `"Z point(s)"`, and `<div class="winner-banner">You won!</div>` when `winner`, delivered live via each player's private Action Cable stream (`game:<id>:player:<player_id>`).
- **Picking Winners** (`N = quiz.number_of_winners`):
  - `"Top N"` (`POST .../pick_top_winners`): marks the first `N` leaderboard players with `points > 0` as winners.
  - `"Draw"` (`POST .../draw_winners`): players with strictly more points than the `N`-th place win automatically; remaining prizes are sampled uniformly at random (`SecureRandom`) from all positive-point players tied at the `N`-th place's point total (ignoring speed). Re-clicking draws fresh winners.
  - Players with `0` points never win; if fewer than `N` players have `points > 0`, all of them win.
  - `"Reset winners"` (`POST .../reset_winners`): clears `winner` on all players.

- **Quiz Settings**: Added `"Timer minutes"` and `"Timer seconds"` number fields (both `0` by default) to Quiz Settings (`Quiz#timer_minutes`, `Quiz#timer_seconds`, where `0` minutes and `0` seconds disables the timer).
